newsitem.title: UK: April UK retail unit trust sales at record level.
newsitem.headline: April UK retail unit trust sales at record level.

text.p: Buyers rushing to beat the tax year end drove British unit trust sales to record heights in April, latest data show.

The Association of Unit Trust and Investment Funds (AUTIF) said on Tuesday net retail sales of unit trusts were 1.6 billion pounds in April, up 498 million pounds from the previous best in April 1996.
April Personal Equity Plan (PEP) net sales of 1.6 billion account for much of the rise, with 797 million pounds sales alone in the first five days as buyers scrambled to beat the end of the tax year.
In order to qualify for the annual capital gains allowance, PEPs must be invested before the close of the tax year.
But strong PEP sales through the balance of April point to a developing trend in retail sales, according to AUTIF.
"Many investors now seem to be getting into a regular habit of using their allowances at the beginning of the tax year," AUTIF's Anne McMeehan said.
Total net investment stood at 2.1 billion pounds in the month, including institutional sales.
PEP buyers have been piling into UK Growth and UK Growth and Income funds, according to AUTIF, with Corporate Bond funds also popular.
Sales of Equity Income funds suffered their fifth consecutive monthly drop.
The Association said unit trust funds under management topped 143 billion pounds and unit trust PEP funds totalled almost 30 billion pounds. - James Saft, London newsroom +171 542 2734
